stories.headline: Applied Materials posts record $9.12B quarter and guides Q4 to $10.25B on AI chip demand

key_facts.fact: Applied Materials reported record fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $9.12 billion on Aug. 13, up 25% year over year, with the highest sequential revenue growth in company history.
key_facts.excerpt: Record revenue $9.12 billion, up 25 percent year over year ... 'Applied Materials delivered another record-breaking quarter, including the highest sequential revenue growth in the company's history,' said Gary Dickerson, President and CEO.

key_facts.fact: GAAP EPS was $3.17 and non-GAAP EPS a record $3.50, up 43% and 41% respectively; net income rose 43% to $2.54 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: GAAP EPS $3.17 and record non-GAAP EPS $3.50, up 43 percent and 41 percent year over year, respectively ... Net income $ 2,538 $ 1,779 43%

key_facts.fact: The company guided fiscal Q4 to about $10.25 billion in revenue, plus or minus $500 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.02 — implying 51% year-over-year revenue growth and 85% EPS growth at the midpoint.
key_facts.excerpt: Applied Materials expects total revenues of approximately $10.25 billion (+/-$500 million), implying 51% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. The company expects non-GAAP earnings of $4.02 per share (+/- 20 cents), indicating 85% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.

key_facts.fact: Semiconductor Systems revenue was $7.04 billion, up 27% year over year, with DRAM including high-bandwidth-memory packaging up 52% and advanced packaging revenue now expected to grow more than 70% in fiscal 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Segment performance was led by Semiconductor Systems, which generated $7.04 billion in revenues, up 27% ... DRAM, including HBM packaging, increased 52% year over year ... now expects advanced packaging revenues to increase more than 70% in fiscal 2026

key_facts.fact: Applied said customers announced more than 10 new fab projects in the quarter and that it plans to double quarterly system manufacturing capacity from current levels by 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Customers announced more than 10 new fab projects in the quarter ... Doubling quarterly system manufacturing capacity from current levels by 2028

key_facts.fact: Despite beating estimates of $3.40 a share, AMAT stock slid in extended trading after the report.
key_facts.excerpt: Applied Materials (AMAT) late Thursday beat analyst estimates for its fiscal third quarter and with its guidance for fiscal Q4. But AMAT stock slid in extended trading.

stories.headline: Lam Research to spend over $3B in five years to expand chip R&D labs, lifting experiment capacity 50%

key_facts.fact: Lam Research announced on Aug. 13 that it intends to invest more than $3 billion over the next five years to expand its global R&D lab network.
key_facts.excerpt: FREMONT, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ: LRCX) today announced that it intends to invest more than $3 billion over the next five years to expand its global research and development (R&D) lab network.

key_facts.fact: The multi-site expansion is expected to increase experiment capacity by more than 50%; Lam's labs currently support more than one million experiments a year across the US, Asia and Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: The planned multi-site expansion is expected to add infrastructure and capabilities to increase experiment capacity by more than 50% ... Lam's global lab network spans the United States, Asia, and Europe. The combined R&D infrastructure supports more than one million experiments annually.

key_facts.fact: CEO Tim Archer framed the spending as a race against AI-era chip complexity: 'Our ability to increase velocity throughout the R&D process has become a decisive advantage.'
key_facts.excerpt: "In the AI era, the pace of innovation is relentless, requiring chips with new architectures, different materials, and complex features engineered with nanoscale precision. Our ability to increase velocity throughout the R&D process has become a decisive advantage," said Tim Archer, president and chief executive officer of Lam Research.

key_facts.fact: Lam says the integrated lab approach has already shortened process development by up to 2.5 times in recent customer engagements, and the expansion starts this year.
key_facts.excerpt: In recent customer engagements, this approach has enabled Lam to shorten process development up to 2.5 times. Lam plans to begin expanding the global lab network this year with the goal of increasing innovation velocity.

key_facts.fact: Lam Research shares rose 10.2% following the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Why Lam Research (LRCX) Is Up 10.2% After $3 Billion Global R&D Lab Expansion Plan

stories.headline: SMIC raises wafer prices for Q3 and says AI orders will keep its fabs full through 2026

key_facts.fact: On an earnings call on Aug. 13-14, SMIC co-CEO Zhao Haijun said the foundry raised prices after negotiations with customers in the first quarter and will charge more for wafers processed in the third quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Co-CEO Zhao Haijun said on an earnings call that SMIC raised prices following negotiations with customers in the first quarter, and that it would charge more for wafers processed in the third quarter.

key_facts.fact: Zhao justified the increases by pointing to the gap with global rivals: 'Since there's still a big gap between industry-leading wafer prices and SMIC's current prices, we need to negotiate with customers for fairer pricing.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We believe we've reached top-tier industry standards in these areas," Zhao said. "Since there's still a big gap between industry-leading wafer prices and SMIC's current prices, we need to negotiate with customers for fairer pricing."

key_facts.fact: SMIC shipped 2.9 million 8-inch-equivalent wafers in Q2, up 14% from the previous quarter, while average selling price per wafer rose 5.7%, pushing quarterly revenue above $3 billion for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: The company shipped 2.9 million 8-inch-equivalent wafers in Q2, up 14% from the previous quarter, while the average selling price of wafers rose 5.7% ... posted revenue above US$3 billion for the first time in the second quarter

key_facts.fact: Zhao said the volume gains came mainly from AI-driven demand for chips other than CPUs and GPUs, mostly from China-based customers, with some orders arriving earlier than scheduled.
key_facts.excerpt: Zhao Haijun attributed the volume gains to accelerating demand for chips used in AI applications outside the traditional CPU and GPU categories, with most orders originating from Chinese customers and some arriving ahead of schedule.

key_facts.fact: China accounted for 90% of SMIC's second-quarter revenue and the US 8%; the company guided third-quarter revenue up 2% to 4% sequentially.
key_facts.excerpt: China remained SMIC's largest market, accounting for 90% of Q2 revenue, while the US contributed 8%. ... SMIC expects Q3 revenue to rise 2% to 4% from Q2, with wafer shipments continuing to increase.

key_facts.fact: SMIC said it will reallocate existing capacity and accelerate the ramp of new production lines to ease supply tightness, and told Nikkei there is 'no chance' it will cut prices despite weak smartphone and auto markets.
key_facts.excerpt: SMIC ... says the artificial intelligence boom is driving massive demand for peripheral AI chips, and that there is "no chance" the company will lower its prices despite weaknesses in the smartphone and automotive markets.

stories.headline: Vantage Data Centers weighs a record $100B data-center IPO or an outright sale

key_facts.fact: Vantage Data Centers, a hyperscale data center developer and operator, is exploring options including an IPO or a sale as soon as next year, Reuters reported on Aug. 13.
key_facts.excerpt: NEW YORK, Aug 13 (Reuters) - Vantage Data Centers, a major hyperscale developer and operator, is exploring options including an IPO or sale as soon as next year, according to people familiar with the matter, as AI-driven demand lifts data center valuations and fuels dealmaking.

key_facts.fact: The company could raise around $10 billion at a valuation of about $100 billion, which would be the largest data center IPO to date; a stake sale is also on the table.
key_facts.excerpt: Vantage, backed by private equity firm Silver Lake and infrastructure investor DigitalBridge Group, could raise around $10 billion and pursue a stock market listing at a valuation of about $100 billion, which would make it the largest data center IPO to date, two of the people said.

key_facts.fact: Discussions are preliminary — no formal process has been launched and Vantage has only met informally with financial advisers in recent weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has held preliminary discussions in recent weeks about possible exit paths and met informally with financial advisers, the sources said. No formal process has been launched, the deliberations remain at an early stage.

key_facts.fact: Vantage has raised roughly $11 billion since late 2023, including a $9.2 billion equity investment led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake.
key_facts.excerpt: Vantage has raised roughly $11 billion since late 2023, including a $9.2 billion equity investment led by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake. The valuation based on those raisings was not disclosed.

key_facts.fact: Vantage recently partnered with Oracle and OpenAI on a Wisconsin data center campus tied to Stargate, the SoftBank-OpenAI-Oracle venture aiming at up to $500 billion and 10 gigawatts.
key_facts.excerpt: Vantage recently partnered with Oracle and OpenAI on a data center campus in Wisconsin tied to Stargate, a joint venture between SoftBank, OpenAI and Oracle to build AI data center infrastructure of up to $500 billion and 10 gigawatts.

key_facts.fact: The move is part of a wave of data-center listings: Switch has hired banks for an IPO that could raise up to $10 billion at about an $80 billion valuation, and CyrusOne is preparing a possible listing as early as 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters reported last month that data center operator Switch had hired banks for an IPO that could raise up to $10 billion and value the company at about $80 billion, while CyrusOne is preparing for a potential IPO as early as 2027.

stories.headline: OpenAI previews Ultrafast tier on Cerebras chips, running GPT-5.6 Sol at 750 tokens per second

key_facts.fact: Cerebras announced on Aug. 13 that it powers Ultrafast mode, a new service tier in the OpenAI API for GPT-5.6 Sol, running at up to 750 output tokens per second and up to 14 times faster than Standard processing.
key_facts.excerpt: SUNNYVALE, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cerebras (NASDAQ: CBRS) today announced that it is powering Ultrafast mode, a new service tier in the OpenAI API for GPT-5.6 Sol. Available initially in limited preview to OpenAI customers, Ultrafast runs GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 output tokens per second and up to 14x faster than Standard processing.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras says Ultrafast delivers the same model quality as Standard, and cites Artificial Analysis data putting it 5x faster than Claude Opus 4.8 in Fast mode and 11x faster than Claude Fable 5.
key_facts.excerpt: Based on output speeds for Anthropic models reported by Artificial Analysis, Ultrafast is 5x faster than Claude Opus 4.8 in Fast mode, and 11x faster than Claude Fable 5.

key_facts.fact: The tier is in limited preview with a small group of OpenAI customers, and access will expand as capacity grows; OpenAI has not published pricing.
key_facts.excerpt: Ultrafast, which is currently being released in preview, is being powered by OpenAI's partnership with chipmaker Cerebras. Currently, that preview is only being made available to a small group of customers, although OpenAI says that it will expand access to the feature as 'capacity grows.'

key_facts.fact: The speed comes from Cerebras' Wafer-Scale Engine architecture and its 44GB of on-chip SRAM, which cuts the data-movement bottlenecks that limit GPU-based inference.
key_facts.excerpt: This new Ultrafast mode is powered by Cerebras' Wafer-Scale Engine architecture, which uses 44GB of on-chip SRAM, reducing the data movement bottlenecks that typically limit inference speeds on GPU-based systems.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras builds dinner-plate-sized processors cut from a single silicon wafer, letting an entire model sit on one chip instead of being split across racks of Nvidia GPUs — a step away from OpenAI's total dependence on Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras builds processors the size of a dinner plate, cut from a single silicon wafer, which lets an entire model sit on one chip rather than being split across racks of Nvidia GPUs that must constantly shuttle data between them ... For OpenAI, leaning on Cerebras is also a quiet step away from total dependence on Nvidia.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI had flagged the Cerebras-served Sol tier when it previewed GPT-5.6, saying it would launch at up to 750 tokens per second in July; the public preview only opened on Aug. 13.
key_facts.excerpt: Back in June, when OpenAI first announced the GPT-5.6 series, the company said that Sol would also launch on Cerebras in July ... However, OpenAI did not reveal any details in July about running Sol inference on the Cerebras platform.

stories.headline: Pony.ai and Uber to put over 2,000 robotaxis in five European cities, with the Middle East next

key_facts.fact: Pony.ai and Uber announced on Aug. 13 an expanded partnership to deploy more than 2,000 Pony.ai robotaxis across Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Pony AI Inc. ('Pony.ai') (NASDAQ: PONY; HKEX: 2026) ... and Uber Technologies, Inc. ('Uber') (NYSE: UBER) today announced an expansion of their strategic partnership, with plans to collaborate on the deployment of more than 2,000 Pony.ai Robotaxis across Europe.

key_facts.fact: The rollout expands from the existing commercial service in Zagreb — coming soon to the Uber app — to four additional European cities, and the deal also includes plans to deploy in the Middle East.
key_facts.excerpt: The partnership will expand from the existing commercial service in Zagreb, coming soon to the Uber platform, to four additional cities in Europe. The expanded partnership also includes plans to deploy Robotaxis in the Middle East.

key_facts.fact: Under the agreement Pony.ai supplies its Level 4 autonomous driving technology and deployment expertise while Uber handles booking, payments and support; local fleet partners run day-to-day operations.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the agreement, Pony.ai will provide its Level 4 autonomous driving technology and deployment expertise, while Uber will offer customer access through its platform, including booking, payments and support. Local fleet partners will handle day-to-day operations in each market.

key_facts.fact: The partnership dates to May 2025; in 2026 the two worked with Croatian mobility company Verne to launch Europe's first commercial robotaxi service in Zagreb, with Verne as local fleet owner and operator.
key_facts.excerpt: The collaboration dates back to May 2025 ... In 2026, the companies worked with Croatian mobility company Verne to launch Europe's first commercial Robotaxi service in Zagreb, with Verne serving as the local fleet owner and operator.

key_facts.fact: Uber's autonomous mobility head Sarfraz Maredia framed the deal as a shift 'from individual launches to repeatable commercial scale.'
key_facts.excerpt: The next chapter for autonomous mobility is about moving from individual launches to repeatable commercial scale," said Sarfraz Maredia, Global Head of Autonomous Mobility & Delivery at Uber.

key_facts.fact: The companies did not disclose which four cities are next; Pony told SiliconRepublic that details will follow in phases.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies did not reveal which locations they plan to focus on, but a Pony spokesperson told SiliconRepublic.com that further details will follow.
